text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on June 24 in history:
79 - Vespasian, Roman emperor from 69-79 and founder of the Flavian dynasty, died.
1314 - Robert the Bruce of Scotland inflicted a crushing defeat against superior English forces under King Edward II at the battle of Bannockburn.
1340 - In the Hundred Years war, the British fleet destroyed the French at Sluys.
1497 - John Cabot, navigator and explorer, sighted Cape Breton Island and claimed North America for England.
1509 - Henry VIII was crowned King of England, the second monarch from the House of Tudor.
1519 - Lucrezia Borgia, Italian noblewoman and a member of the infamous Borgia family of the Italian Renaissance, died.
1793 - During the French revolution, the Constitution of Year One of the Republic was approved.
1812 - Napoleon, leading his Grand Armee, began his invasion of Russia.
1850 - Horatio Herbert Kitchener, British conqueror of Sudan, born. Appointed Secretary of War, he undertook the organisation of the British army for World War One.
1859 - Napoleon III defeated the Austrians at the Battle of Solferinfo in Lombardy. Henri Dunant, who organised relief for the thousands wounded there, later founded the Red Cross in 1864.
1866 - In the Seven Weeks War, the Austrians scored a notable victory over the Italians in the second Battle of Custozza.
1901 - The first exhibition by the 19-year-old Pablo Picasso opened in Paris to high critical acclaim.
1904 - U.S. bandleader Phil Harris born; he also achieved stardom providing voices for Disney cartoons notably "The Jungle Book".
1908 - Grover Cleveland, twice U.S. president (1885-89 and 1893-97), died.
1916 - The First Battle of the Somme began. It lasted five months and the death toll of over one million was for the sake of an allied advance of 125 square miles.
1930 - French film director Claude Chabrol born. Best known for his successful thrillers including "Que la Bete Meure" and "La Ceremonie".
1940 - France signed an armistice with Italy in World War Two.
1940 - Japan formally asked Britain to close the Burma Road.
1941 - The Germans advanced into Russia and took Vilna, Brest-Litovsk and Kaunas.
1947 - An American pilot reported seeing strange objects in the sky looking like "saucers skipping across the water". This incident led to the first use of the term "flying saucers".
1948 - The Russians began a blockade of Berlin, stopping all land traffic and food from entering the city from West Germany.
1963 - As a step towards independence, Zanzibar achieved internal self-government.
1967 - A referendum in Zaire, in which women voted for the first time, approved a new constitution.
1970 - Alexander Dubcek, former leader of Czechoslovakia whose reforms led to the Soviet invasion in 1968, was dismissed from his post as ambassador to Turkey.
1973 - Eamon de Valera, the world's oldest statesman resigned as president of Ireland at the age of 90.
1975 - A U.S. Eastern Airlines Boeing 727 crashed near Kennedy Airport, killing 113 people out of 124 aboard.
1978 - The President of the Yemen Arab Republic, Lieut-Colonel Ahmed Hussein al-Ghashni, was killed by a parcel bomb.
1983 - Yasser Arafat was ordered to leave Syria by President Assad.
1987 - In South Korea, Kim Dae-Jung and 300 other dissidents were released after two weeks of unrest in the country.
1989 - Zhao Ziyang, who had expressed sympathy with pro-democracy students, was replaced by Jiang Zemin as general Secretary of the Communist Party.
